authors: Microsoft, Alexey, Jonas, Imran and the Power Platform community
description:
Register and manage plug-ins, custom workflow activities, steps, images, plug-in packages, webhooks, Azure service endpoints and Custom APIs in Microsoft Dataverse and Dynamics 365.

			Based on the classic Plug-in Registration Tool that Microsoft published as a Dynamics CRM 2011 SDK sample, ported to XrmToolBox and extended by the community.
releaseNotes:
New: Azure service endpoints
- #36: Register and update service endpoints from the Register menu: Service Bus queues and topics, Event Hubs, one-way, two-way and REST relays, and Event Grid, with a SAS key, SAS token or access key, message format and user claim. Update and Export no longer fail on a service endpoint
- #36: When editing an endpoint, keys and tokens left empty keep their saved values. The namespace address can be entered as a host name or an https address
- #36: Steps on a service endpoint show under it, can be registered from its context menu, also with managed assemblies hidden, and can have images
- Endpoints that Dataverse manages itself, such as Managed Data Lake, can't be edited, unregistered or given steps
- Webhooks and service endpoints have their own icons, and the properties pane only shows the fields that apply to the endpoint's type

New: Custom APIs
- #173: Register, edit and delete Custom APIs together with their request parameters and response properties, from the Register menu or an API's context menu. Fields that Dataverse fixes after creation are read-only, and managed APIs are protected (thanks @WebbontheWeb)
- #173: View > Display by Custom API (Ctrl+Shift+C) lists the Custom APIs, also those without steps, with the steps on each API's message beneath it. Managed APIs are hidden until you turn off Hide Managed Custom APIs on the toolbar. Custom APIs have their own icon, an envelope with a gear
- #173: A new API is created in an unmanaged solution that you pick or create, with the publisher prefix applied to its unique name. Parameters added later join the solutions the API is in
- #173: Add to Solution adds an API with all its parameters and properties in one go
- #173: Steps can be registered and edited on private Custom APIs
- The bound table and execute privilege are searchable lists: type part of a table's logical or display name, or of a privilege name. Both are read once per connection; Reload choices reads them again, for example after adding a table. Names that aren't listed can still be typed
- The plug-in assembly and plug-in type are searchable too, and show the assembly version, so assemblies with the same name in different major versions can be told apart
- Register New Step: Message and Primary Entity are searchable lists. Custom API messages are marked "Custom API", so typing "custom api" lists them, and "none" says whether it means all tables or no table
- Register New Step: on the message of a Custom API that allows only asynchronous steps, the step is set to asynchronous Post-operation, with a note saying why
- Register New Image is greyed out on a step whose message can't have images, such as a Custom API's, and its tooltip says why. The image dialog says the same for the selected step and links to Microsoft's list of the messages that support images

New: managed identities (Dataverse online only)
- Link a managed identity to a plug-in assembly or package from its context menu or the toolbar, and create, edit or delete identities from the same dialog. New identities use version 2, which Microsoft recommends. Based on Plugin Identity Manager by David Rivard (https://github.com/drivardxrm/Driv.XTB.PluginIdentityManager), with thanks
- The properties pane shows the linked identity of an assembly or package

UX & stability improvements, bug fixes
- #16: Updating an assembly now brings in arguments added to its custom workflow activities. Dataverse only reads an activity's arguments again when its plug-in type comes with the update, so the workflow designer used to keep showing the old ones
- #16: Before such an update, the tool compares each workflow activity's arguments with the registered ones. If an argument is removed, changes type or becomes required, it lists those changes and asks before updating, since processes that use them may fail. Added optional arguments go through without a question
- The Update button has a new icon at the toolbar's size, instead of the old small one blown up
- Sharper icons in the tree and on the Enable/Disable button: they were squeezed to 16 pixels in 256 colours, and are now full colour and a little larger, growing with Windows display scaling
- Register New Step is only offered where a step can go: on a plug-in, service endpoint, webhook, message or Custom API. Register New Image is only offered on a step, and the dialog opens with that step selected. Menus, toolbar and shortcuts follow the same rule
- New images on Create steps have Post Image ticked, with a tooltip explaining why a Create step can't have a pre-image
- #145: A fast double-click on a checkbox in the Register New Assembly dialog no longer leaves the assembly ticked and its plug-ins unticked
- Registering an assembly no longer fails at random with "Index was outside the bounds of the array"
- Register New Custom API is no longer offered on webhook and service endpoint nodes
- #175: Each connection now shows its own SDK messages. After changing connection, or with the tool open in two tabs, the step editor used to offer the messages of the first environment (thanks @WebbontheWeb)
- #175: Refresh (F5) retries a failed load, and a failed refresh keeps the current tree instead of closing the connection
- #175: Registration commands are disabled while the organization is loading
- #175: Editing a step whose message isn't available, such as a private message, explains why instead of failing
- #148: Creating or updating a plug-in package shows a wait cursor and locks the dialog until the upload has finished
- #15: Unregistering shows a wait cursor, and the progress bar in the XrmToolBox status bar now advances with the work
- Unregistering runs in the background behind the XrmToolBox wait box, which shows how far it has got, so XrmToolBox no longer freezes on an assembly with many plug-ins. If a delete fails partway, the tree is reloaded to show what is left
- An assembly or plug-in that is part of a plug-in package can no longer be unregistered on its own. Dataverse deleted its plug-in types and only then refused to delete the assembly; the tool now refuses before anything is deleted
- The plug-in package dialog shows the XrmToolBox wait box while it registers or updates a package
- #100: Editing a webhook keeps its header, query string or key values when you leave them empty. Dataverse never returns them, so the dialog now says so instead of showing an empty list. Values with quotes, & or < are saved correctly

Security
- #178: Removed the unused System.Security.Cryptography.Pkcs reference, which had two denial-of-service advisories (GHSA-846f-f764-76mx, GHSA-2fmv-rv2c-59x7)
summary: Register plug-ins, steps, images, webhooks, service endpoints and Custom APIs in Dataverse, from XrmToolBox
title: Plugin Registration for XrmToolBox
